749: 2 Supplement. Definition of SQS and generation tools
750: An SQS (Special Quasirandom Structure) is a finite periodic structure in which the atomic species are arranged so that the cluster correlations within a chosen finite range come close to those of a perfectly random alloy. It is neither a mere random arrangement nor the lowest-energy structure. What was called “chemical” here means “which element occupies each lattice site”, as distinct from the thermal vibrations and displacements of the atoms. In the rest of this document the SQS of element occupation is simply called SQS.
